prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No AI coach is shown to help people form lasting habits, and none reaches 1,000,000,000 people, so the Main KPI is unmet. The trial evidence for AI habit coaching is thin: a GPT habit coach was piloted with 5 people for five days (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.19229), a four-week LLM coach study with 54 people measured enjoyment rather than habit formation (https://arxiv.org/html/2510.05449v1), and a six-month LLM coaching RCT was still awaiting ethics approval (https://anzctr.org.au/ACTRN12625000412437p.aspx). Health and habit apps keep only about 3 to 8 percent of users at day 30 (https://martechvibe.com/?p=32648), and in the founding habit study only 23 percent of participants reached automaticity (https://www.thebehavioralscientist.com/articles/how-long-to-form-a-habit). Existing reach is commercial or small: Noom reports about 45 million users, while open-source Habitica is far smaller (https://sp-edge.com/companies/45510). Honest limit: habit-tracking apps and general chatbots are known answers; only lasting, measured habit change at scale is open.
